cards.lore: Protecting the airway is the prime directive. Upper Airway compromise demands the Tube-Tango (Intubation) to prevent asphyxiation.
cards.power: Annie ensures oxygen reaches the lungs. If blocked by debris or a swollen tongue, the match ends in minutes.

cards.lore: Focus on tension. If obstructive pressure pushes the heart aside, the Needle-Decompression-Nudge restores ventilation.
cards.power: Ben manages the gas exchange. If the chest isn't rising, Ben deploys the BVM-Bag or the Chest-Tube-Chisel.

cards.lore: Shock is a failure of perfusion. Deploy the Two Large-Bore strategy to keep organs from dying of thirst.
cards.power: Cyril manages the pressure pipes. If the blood leaks or the pump stalls, Cyril initiates fluid-flooding.

cards.lore: Always check the sugar! A low glucose crash mimics a stroke but only needs a Dextrose-Drop to be defeated.
cards.power: Dave checks the Mainframe. If pupils differ or both are blown, suspect a massive bleed.

cards.lore: Vinnie needs the Electrical-Reset-Button. Defibrillation stops the chaos so the natural pacemaker can regain command.
cards.power: Vinnie makes the heart quiver like a bag of worms. Zero blood moves.

cards.lore: You cannot shock a dead battery. Fred requires high-quality CPR and the Epi-Injection-Engine every 3-5 minutes.
cards.power: Fred is the absence of life. He cannot be shocked.

cards.lore: Unstable? Synchronized-Zap. Stable? Adenosine-Reset.
cards.power: Tony runs the heart so fast that the filling chambers never have time to load blood.

cards.lore: Usually a wiring issue. Atropine might speed him up, but an external battery (Pacing) is the real fix.
cards.power: Bill makes the heart beat so slowly that the brain blacks out from lack of pressure.

cards.lore: Triggered by allergens. Epinephrine is the only key to constrict the pipes and open the lungs simultaneously.
cards.power: Annie turns blood vessels into sieves and slams the airway door shut with explosive edema.

cards.lore: Sam demands the Hour-1-Bundle: massive fluids, cultures, and early Pressor-Power (Norepinephrine).
cards.power: Sam uses a Cytokine-Tsunami to paralyze blood vessels, causing total pressure collapse.

cards.lore: Fluid is the enemy. Carl needs Inotrope-Ignition to boost pump strength and an immediate trip to the Cath Lab.
cards.power: Carl fails to push. Blood backs up into the lungs, drowning the patient from the inside.

cards.lore: Replace what is lost! If it's blood, give blood. If it's water, give crystalloids.
cards.power: Hank strikes when volume is missing. There simply isn't enough juice left to keep the lights on.

cards.lore: The king of the Code Blue. He diverts all remaining blood to the brain and heart during the fight.
cards.power: Eric violently constricts the pipes and screams at the heart to beat faster.

cards.lore: A Class III antiarrhythmic. It buys critical time for the heart to find its normal beat again.
cards.power: Ami stabilizes the heart's electrical wires to keep the static storm of V-Fib from returning.

cards.lore: An anticholinergic assassin. She stops the Rest and Digest system from ending the match prematurely.
cards.power: Alice cuts the Vagus-Brake, completely removing the inhibitory signals slowing down the heart.

cards.lore: Used for SVT. It feels like a massive thump in the chest to the conscious patient.
cards.power: Andy stops the heart completely for a few terrifying seconds, forcing it to reboot into a normal rhythm.

cards.lore: A clinical diagnosis! Do not wait for X-Ray. Execute the Needle-Decompression-Nudge in the 5th intercostal Space immediately.
cards.power: Tony traps air in the chest on a one-way valve, building pressure until the Great Vessels are squashed flat.

cards.lore: Beware the short half-life. Nancy might wear off before the opiates do, throwing the patient back into a coma.
cards.power: Nancy violently rips opiates off the brain's receptors, bringing the patient back to life instantly.

cards.lore: Beyond low sugar, Gwen is the secret key to restart the engine during a lethal Beta-Blocker overdose.
cards.power: Gwen forces the liver to dump its entire emergency stash of sugar into the blood.

cards.lore: Reduces mortality in Myocardial Infarction by preventing the Clot-Monster from growing any larger.
cards.power: Ace makes the blood-clotters slippery so they can't block the Coronary-Canyons.

cards.lore: A true emergency. Harry requires immediate, aggressive physical cooling (ice water/fans) before the brain permanently melts.
cards.power: Harry cooks the body's proteins from the inside out. Sweat production has utterly failed.

cards.lore: Nobody is dead until they are warm and dead! Frank requires extremely careful, active internal rewarming.
cards.power: Frank slows cellular time down to a crawl until the heart stumbles into fatal V-Fib.

cards.lore: Hypoxia is the ultimate killer. Drake requires immediate ventilation and high PEEP to flush fluid out of the alveoli.
cards.power: Drake fills the fragile lungs with water, or triggers an iron-tight spasm of the vocal cords to lock air out.

cards.lore: Massive volume loss is the silent threat. Ben requires enormous amounts of Ringer's Lactate in the first 24 hours.
cards.power: Ben destroys the skin shield. Core water evaporates instantly, and bacterial armies march in.

cards.lore: The patient suffocates despite ample oxygen in the room. Carl demands 100% O2 or a hyperbaric pressure chamber.
cards.power: Carl binds to the oxygen bus 240 times stronger than O2. The pulse oximeter lies to you.

cards.lore: Otto requires massive, repeated doses of Atropine-Alice until the lungs are finally dry.
cards.power: Otto blocks the cleanup of nerve signals; the entire parasympathetic system is stuck on Full Fire.

cards.lore: If standard Atropine fails to break the lock, Gluca-Gwen is the chemical bypass key needed to restart the engine.
cards.power: Ben suppresses the beta-receptors, slowing the heart's rate and squeeze down so much that it nearly stalls.

cards.lore: The specific antidote is Sodium Bicarbonate—it floods the channels with sodium to flush Ty out and stabilize the wires.
cards.power: Ty blocks crucial sodium channels, widening the QRS complex and throwing the heart into a deadly cardiac rhythm.

cards.lore: During CPR, the uterus must be manually shifted to the left, otherwise compressions are pumping an empty heart.
cards.power: The heavy uterus physically crushes the Inferior Vena Cava when lying flat, preventing blood from returning to the heart.

cards.lore: Ventilation is the absolute priority. Airway management saves pediatric lives before the heart ever stops.
cards.power: In children, cardiac arrest is rarely a primary pump failure; it is almost always driven by fatal hypoxia.

cards.lore: Damage Control Resuscitation: Keep them warm, stop the bleed, avoid crystalloids, and pump high ratios of blood products.
cards.power: Tanya alters blood physics: blood absolutely refuses to clot when the body gets cold and acidic.

cards.lore: Manual CPR fatigue rescuers instantly. Mechanical CPR devices and advanced airway planning are mandatory here.
cards.power: Oliver's sheer mass makes achieving adequate chest compression depth and effective ventilation a monumental physical ordeal.

cards.lore: Dan discharges every cardiac cell simultaneously, creating a moment of total silence so the pacemaker can restart the beat.
cards.power: Dan sends a violently controlled electrical punch directly through the heart muscle to end all chaotic activity.

cards.lore: Avoid gastric inflation! Squeezing Bill too hard forces air into the stomach, guaranteeing a vomit tsunami.
cards.power: Bill forcefully presses oxygen down into the lungs when the patient's own bellows fail.

cards.lore: The bone marrow is a non-collapsible vein. Anything you can push in an IV, you can push through Iggy.
cards.power: When peripheral veins collapse into hiding, Iggy violently drills a direct fluid highway right into the bone marrow.

cards.lore: Larry is the essential scouting tool required for Airway-Annie to successfully place the Golden Tube.
cards.power: Larry physically wrestles the heavy tongue out of the way, lighting a path through the dark tunnel to the vocal cords.

cards.lore: Time is Brain! Steve demands either the Clot-Dissolver (Lyse) or the Mechanical Grabber (Thrombectomy) immediately.
cards.power: Steve blocks a vital arterial supply line in the head. Every passing minute, millions of neurons permanently die.

cards.lore: Sidus needs GABA-Garry (Benzodiazepines) immediately to extinguish the runaway electrical fire.
cards.power: Sidus forces the brain to fire at maximum capacity uncontrollably, burning incredible energy and risking permanent melting.

cards.lore: The Brawler triggers the Cushing Reflex (High BP, Low Pulse) as the brain desperately fights to push blood against the rising crush.
cards.power: The Brawler leaks expanding blood into the rigid skull. Because the bone won't yield, intracranial pressure spikes instantly.

cards.lore: The brain needs glucose like a car needs gas. Without juice, the engine completely stalls. Always check the sugar!
cards.power: Harry flawlessly disguises himself as Stroke-Steve or Seizure-Sidus, tricking medics until sugar reveals his true identity.

cards.lore: A positive Fiona signal in a hemodynamically unstable trauma patient is a direct, one-way ticket to the operating room.
cards.power: Fiona shoots high-frequency sound to hunt down hidden, pooling blood in the belly or trapped around the heart in seconds.

cards.lore: High Larry means occult shock is happening at the cellular level, regardless of how normal the blood pressure currently looks.
cards.power: Larry acts as the cellular distress signal, revealing exactly how badly the tissues are starving and crying for oxygen.

cards.lore: Troy is highly specific—if you find these nuggets in the bloodstream, you have absolute proof of a Myocardial Infarction.
cards.power: Troy is exclusively released when cardiac muscle cells are actively dying and breaking apart.

cards.lore: Bella is the ultimate high-fidelity dashboard for fine-tuning mechanical ventilation and targeted fluid resuscitation.
cards.power: Bella reveals the invisible metabolic scale: is the wrestler acidic or basic, and are the lungs or the kidneys to blame?

cards.lore: Normal medical ethics invert here. The ultimate goal is the survival of the many, not the desperate rescue of the individual.
cards.power: In mass casualty chaos, Raven makes the ruthless, split-second decisions about who gets the limited medical resources.

cards.lore: Treat as you go. But critical bleeding and airway obstruction are always addressed before the wheels roll.
cards.power: The ultimate operational fork: Immediate, frantic transport for surgery bleeding, versus methodical on-scene stabilization for medical codes.

cards.lore: Heidi radically expands the geographical capture radius for highly time-sensitive interventions (Stroke Centers / Level 1 Trauma).
cards.power: Heidi completely bypasses ground traffic, bringing the highest level of specialized doctor and equipment directly to the dirt.

cards.lore: Respect the Log Roll. The patient must be turned as a single, rigid tree trunk to avoid permanently angering Chris.
cards.power: Chris ensures that the fragile spinal cord isn't shredded by unstable, shattered vertebrae during rescue movements.

cards.lore: A dropped baton is lethal. A poor Hank kills the patient through hospital ignorance and delayed interventions.
cards.power: Hank perfectly transfers critical field knowledge from the muddy EMS team to the sterile shock room without dropping a byte.

cards.lore: Without the Sgt commanding the room from the foot of the bed, the high-tech shock room instantly degrades into a noisy chicken coop.
cards.power: The Sgt coordinates trauma surgeons, anesthesiologists, and nurses in a perfectly choreographed, silent dance.

cards.lore: Clear fluids only dilute clotting factors. In massive hemorrhage, only blood replaces blood.
cards.power: When Hypovolemic-Hank drains the blood, the Tank re-enters the system, refilling the wrestler with actual, life-saving hemoglobin and platelets.

cards.lore: The post-resuscitation phase is incredibly critical: the war is won, but the assassins will return if the Ranger isn't violently aggressive.
cards.power: The Ranger stands guard, monitoring the chaotic equilibrium after the Golden Hour Gauntlet has been violently survived.

cards.lore: Treat the life-threats, not the labs. If the pump is dry, fill it. If air is trapped, vent it. Stay fluffy!
cards.power: Cuts through the noise. Operates on pure clinical instinct backed by hardcore physiological lore.

cards.lore: Which intervention clears the blood from the pericardial sac before the pump stalls forever?
cards.power: Identify the mechanical stopper (Tamponade) squeezing the heart.

cards.lore: Who secures the way (Airway-Annie) and who breaks the fatal allergic reaction (Epi-Eric)?
cards.power: Activate the ABCDE sequence under maximum stress.

cards.lore: Name the rhythm (V-Fib). Compress, shock, or push drugs? You have 5 seconds to decide. Go!
cards.power: The ultimate algorithmic decision tree.

title: The Golden Hour Gauntlet — Resuscitation, Rhythms & The Triage Tempest
